contribution_types.label: UNKNOWN: no contribution-type taxonomy published for the ICML 2025 main track
contribution_types.scope: The main track publishes no contribution categories; position papers form a separate submission type.
contribution_types.quote: Similar to last year, we also invite submissions of position papers.

review_criteria.name: Claims and Evidence
review_criteria.official_explanation: Are the paper’s claims supported by clear and convincing evidence, sound methods and correct proofs?
review_criteria.quote: Are the claims made in the submission supported by clear and convincing evidence?

review_criteria.name: Relation to Prior Works
review_criteria.official_explanation: How the key contributions relate to the broader scientific literature and whether essential related work is cited.
review_criteria.quote: How are the key contributions of the paper related to the broader scientific literature?

review_criteria.name: Originality
review_criteria.official_explanation: Originality may arise from creative combinations, removing restrictive assumptions, or real-world application.
review_criteria.quote: originality may arise from creative combinations of existing ideas, removing restrictive assumptions from prior theoretical results, or application to a real-world use case

review_criteria.name: Significance
review_criteria.official_explanation: The work must be of significant interest to the machine learning community.
review_criteria.quote: Submissions should report original and rigorous research of significant interest to the machine learning community.

review_criteria.name: Reproducibility
review_criteria.official_explanation: Claims must be supported by reproducible experiments or sound theoretical analysis.
review_criteria.quote: All claims must be clearly stated and supported by reproducible experiments and/or sound theoretical analysis.

review_criteria.name: Ethical Issues
review_criteria.official_explanation: Reviewers flag papers with ethical issues for ethics review.
review_criteria.quote: If you believe there are ethical issues with this paper, please flag the paper for an ethics review.

review_criteria.name: Submission Compliance
review_criteria.official_explanation: Papers not conforming to ICML submission policies are rejected without review.
review_criteria.quote: Submitted papers that do not conform to these policies will be rejected without review.

mandatory_policy.statement: At least one author of an accepted paper must attend in person to present it, barring exceptional circumstances.
mandatory_policy.quote: We require that, barring exceptional circumstances, at least one of the authors of accepted papers attend the conference in person to present the paper .
mandatory_policy.conditions: Exceptional circumstances may excuse in-person attendance.

mandatory_policy.statement: The main paper is limited to eight pages, with unlimited references, impact statement and appendices.
mandatory_policy.quote: 8 pages for the main paper, with unlimited pages for references, the impact statement, and appendices.

mandatory_policy.statement: All submissions must be anonymized and must not violate double-blind reviewing.
mandatory_policy.quote: All submissions must be anonymized and may not contain any information with the intention or consequence of violating the double-blind reviewing policy.

mandatory_policy.statement: Qualified authors are required to review for ICML.
mandatory_policy.quote: Qualified authors are required to review for ICML, according to the policies below.

mandatory_policy.statement: Authors must include a broader-impact statement covering ethical aspects and societal consequences.
mandatory_policy.quote: Authors are required to include a statement of the potential broader impact of their work, including its ethical aspects and future societal consequences.

recommended_practice.statement: Reviewers are encouraged to be open-minded about potential strengths when assessing originality.
recommended_practice.quote: We encourage you to be open-minded in terms of potential strengths.

recommended_practice.statement: Reviewers should reserve questions for cases that would change their evaluation.
recommended_practice.quote: Please reserve your questions for cases where the response would likely change your evaluation

recommended_practice.statement: Authors are encouraged to explain notable ways generative-AI tools were used in their research methodology.
recommended_practice.quote: We encourage authors to explain any notable ways in which these tools were used in their research methodology.

compliance_checks.requirement: Main body is at most eight pages.
Submission conforms to ICML author policies and style files.
A separate broader-impact section is present.
No identical or substantially similar work under parallel review.
No unaddressed ethical issues in the submission.

changes_from_prior_year.change: ICML 2025 newly requires qualified authors to serve as reviewers, including a per-submission designation and a per-author requirement.
ICML 2025 newly requires accepted papers to supply a lay (plain-language) summary at camera-ready.
Material changes relative to ICML 2024 could not be established.

unknown_policies.question: What changed between ICML 2024 and ICML 2025?
unknown_policies.reason: No ICML 2024 source is cited by this profile, and no prior-year rule may be borrowed.

unknown_policies.question: What were the detailed ICML 2025 rules on generative-AI use?
unknown_policies.reason: The 2025 CFP states only that AI is allowed, that authors are responsible for content, and that LLMs cannot be authors; no separate 2025 LLM policy page was captured.
